name: Dutasteride
description: A dual type I and type II 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor approved for benign prostatic hyperplasia, producing more complete dihydrotestosterone suppression than finasteride and with a much longer half-life.

systems.note: Dual isoenzyme blockade lowers scalp dihydrotestosterone; hair growth is the intended effect of off-label use in the US, where the label covers benign prostatic hyperplasia only.
Reduction of prostatic dihydrotestosterone and prostate volume is the labelled indication.
Dual isoenzyme blockade of testosterone to DHT conversion.
Roughly halves serum PSA; labelled instruction is to double the measured value.
Depression and sexual adverse effects appear in labelling.
Extensively hepatically metabolised; transaminase elevation is reported.

monitors.why: Serum PSA is roughly halved; the labelled instruction is to interpret against that.
Percent free PSA is unchanged by dutasteride, so unlike total PSA it needs no doubling to be read — it is the one PSA value the drug leaves interpretable as it stands.
Testosterone rises as conversion is blocked.
More testosterone is available for aromatisation.
Extensive hepatic metabolism with a very long half-life.
